items.title: OpenAI releases GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol
items.summary: OpenAI released two new models: GPT-6.2 Astra for your hardest projects and GPT-6.2 Sol for everyday work. OpenAI says both get better results while using fewer output tokens, so you can get more done within your usage limits, and that Astra's slides, spreadsheets and documents follow your templates more closely. They are available to Plus, Pro, Enterprise and Edu users in ChatGPT Work and Codex, and to developers through the API.
items.whyItMatters: If you pay for ChatGPT, the models behind longer work tasks just got an upgrade. The launch post does not list the Free plan.

items.title: Google makes Tasks in Gemini free in six countries
items.summary: Google is rolling out Tasks in Gemini free of charge to hundreds of millions of people in the US, Japan, Korea, Canada, Australia and India, running on Gemini 4 Hydrogen. You flip the home-screen toggle from Chat to Task and Gemini works on the job in the background, for example calling businesses, adding dates to your calendar or comparing products. Google says it is designed to check with you before critical steps like buying, and that it can still make mistakes.
items.whyItMatters: It is a free way to hand an AI a real errand rather than just a question. Ireland and the rest of Europe are not in the first countries listed.

items.title: Microsoft makes Copilot Home and Office in Copilot generally available
items.summary: At Ignite 2026, Microsoft said Home, where Copilot Chat and Cowork come together, and Office in Copilot, which brings Word, Excel and PowerPoint into the Copilot app, are now generally available. Copilot Code, which builds simple apps and dashboards from a plain-words description, follows in the coming weeks, and the Autopilot agent is starting to roll out to Frontier customers.
items.whyItMatters: If your workplace uses Microsoft Copilot, you get one starting screen where you can ask a quick question or hand off a whole task.

items.title: Meta's Muse personal agent launches in Australia
items.summary: Meta made Muse, its personal AI agent, available in Australia on iOS, Android, muse.ai and a Mac app. It can connect to services such as Gmail, Google Calendar and OpenTable, with local partners like Canva and Officeworks rolling out over time. Meta says Muse is free for most of what people need and checks with you before sensitive actions such as sending an email or making a purchase.
items.whyItMatters: Agents that do tasks for you, not just answer, are reaching more countries. Asking before sending or buying is a safeguard worth looking for in any agent you try.

items.title: Apple explains daily limits for Siri AI and Apple Intelligence
items.summary: Apple published a support page saying some Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features that rely on server models have a daily limit on each device. Everyday Siri requests like setting a timer still work after you hit it; more complex requests pause until the limit resets, around midnight, or until you move to an iCloud+ plan of 200 GB or more, which gives up to 2x to 20x the standard limit, starting with the 27.3 release.
items.whyItMatters: Heavy Siri AI users may be asked to upgrade iCloud+. Apple says this extra access is not available in the EU or UK.
